Motorcycle Trip Dossier

Rangeley Loop

Waltham → the White Mountains → Rangeley Lakes → back home

Sept 4–62026
3 days2 nights
~510 mibackroads only
2×Honda Rebel

A three-day, non-highway loop built around a strict 2-hour-leg cadence — 3 riding legs a day (breakfast → lunch → dinner), each capped around 55–60 miles at realistic twisty-backroad pace (~28–30 mph average, not car-routing speed). Covers the Kancamagus, Hurricane Mountain Road, and the Maine shore road through Yarmouth and Freeport — with no road repeated across the three days.

Saturday · Sept 5 · Depart 8–9am

Kancamagus, Hurricane Mountain Rd & the Maine Coast

Lincoln, NH → Kancamagus Hwy → Conway, NH → Hurricane Mountain Rd → Bethel, ME → Rt 26 → Falmouth/Yarmouth/Freeport (shore road) → Brunswick, ME

Route map

🗺️ Open Interactive Map in Google Maps ↗

Leg breakdown

  • Leg 1 — Kancamagus, late breakfast~35 mi · ~55m
  • Leg 2 — Hurricane Mountain Rd, lunch, mandatory fill-up~50 mi · ~1h35m
  • Leg 3 — Rt 26 to the coast~90 mi · ~2h
  • Leg 4 — shore road, dinner/overnight~10 mi · ~20m

Stops along the way

  • Conway, NHgas
  • Hurricane Mountain Rdscenic, narrow & twisty
  • Bethel, MEgaslunchfill up — mandatory
  • Freeport, MEshore road, L.L. Bean, Winslow Park
  • Brunswick, MEovernight

Logistics to keep in mind

  • New plan: after today's Kancamagus/Hurricane Mountain Rd catch-up, heads east to the Maine coast instead of Evans Notch/North Conway.
  • Colonial Motel, North Conway needs to be cancelled — overnight moves to Brunswick, ME instead.
  • Fill up fully in Bethel — services thin out before Portland.
  • Hurricane Mountain Road is paved but narrow, patchy, and twisty with real elevation change — take it easy, loaded down with luggage.
  • ~185 miles total — the day's longest, but Leg 3 runs on faster state road (Rt 26), not backroads.
  • New lodging needed in Brunswick, ME — nothing booked here yet.

Hotel options in Brunswick, ME — for you to review

The Brunswick Hotel Boutique hotel 4 Noble St, downtown on Maine St, adjacent to Bowdoin College. OneSixtyFive Inn Historic inn 165 Park Row, downtown — Main House rooms or self check-in Carriage House. Comfort Inn Brunswick Hotel · budget-friendly 199 Pleasant St, under 2 mi from Maine St, free hot breakfast.

3SUN

Sunday · Sept 6 · Depart 8–9am

The Seacoast Way Home

Brunswick, ME → Cape Elizabeth → Old Orchard Beach → Kennebunkport → Ogunquit → York → Portsmouth, NH → Newburyport & the North Shore → Gloucester → 12 Lincoln St, Waltham

Route map

🗺️ Open Interactive Map in Google Maps ↗

Leg breakdown

  • Leg 1 — Cape Elizabeth, breakfast~35 mi · ~1h
  • Leg 2 — beach towns, lunch~30 mi · ~1h15m
  • Leg 3 — York to Portsmouth, gas~30 mi · ~1h15m
  • Leg 4 — North Shore, dinner~45 mi · ~1h30m
  • Leg 5 — arrival home~40 mi · ~1h

Stops along the way

  • Brunswick, MEgas before departure
  • Cape Elizabeth, MEPortland Head Light
  • Kennebunkport, MElunch
  • York, MEgas
  • Portsmouth, NHsnack
  • Newburyport, MAgas
  • Gloucester, MAdinner
  • 12 Lincoln St, Walthamarrival

Logistics to keep in mind

  • Hugs the water the whole way — Cape Elizabeth, the York County beach towns, the NH seacoast, and the MA North Shore (Newburyport, Gloucester, Marblehead) — so you'll see ocean from the road most of the day.
  • This is longer than the original plan — ~180 mi vs. ~141 mi, and slower than the mileage suggests: it's Labor Day Sunday, so expect heavy beach traffic through Old Orchard Beach, Wells, Ogunquit, York, and Hampton. Consider an earlier 7am departure to build in a buffer.
  • Small unavoidable overlap with Saturday's road through Yarmouth/Freeport leaving Brunswick — everything from Cape Elizabeth on is fresh road.
  • Gloucester → Waltham cuts inland for the final stretch since Waltham itself isn't on the coast.

Packing the T-Bag

  • Bottom / center, near the seat: tools, tire kit, toiletries — the heavy stuff, kept low and centered so it doesn't affect handling.
  • Top roll: clothing — light, compressible, fine to sit higher.
  • Outer pocket: rain gear, snacks, charging cable — anything you want at a gas stop without digging through the whole bag.
